title: AI Frontiers in Trust and Safety  Combatting Multifaceted Harm on Tinder at Scale: Vibhor Kumar

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's core technical content is parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA) of open-source LLMs for T&S violation detection, with LoRAX serving as the deployment mechanism for the resulting adapters. Trust and Safety at Tinder is an enterprise operational function, and detecting and mitigating platform harm such as scams and hate speech constitutes security operations and defense. The talk traces the full pipeline from hybrid human-AI data generation through PEFT fine-tuning, production deployment via LoRAX, and ongoing monitoring of adversarial model degradation. The talk assumes familiarity with LLMs, fine-tuning concepts, classification tasks, and open-source ML libraries as stated in the prerequisites. Recorded live conference talk at the AI Engineer World's Fair in San Francisco. All eight evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript, drawn directly from the talk transcript.

summary: Vibhor Kumar, a senior AI engineer at Tinder with five years in trust and safety, outlines how Tinder uses LLMs to detect many categories of harm at global real-time scale. Trust and Safety, framed via Del Harvey's goals (preventing/reducing risk, detecting/mitigating harm), focuses here on detecting harm. Tinder faces a long tail of violations ranging from high-prevalence/low-harm (social media in profiles) to low-prevalence/high-harm (hate speech, harassment, pig butchering scams, underage users). Generative AI introduces problems: content pollution, copyright inheritance, deepfake-enabled catfishing and revenge porn, and scalable automated scam operations that defeat similarity/hash-based signals, pushing T&S toward metadata signals. However, opportunities abound: open-source pretrained LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral) offer latent semantic capability and global language coverage; fine-tuning achieves SOTA performance, sometimes beating few-shot GPT-4; mature open-source tooling accelerates development from months to weeks; and LLM generalization slows adversarial degradation. The training data pipeline uses a text-in/text-out format with wrapped prompts and classification labels. A hybrid approach uses GPT-4 with clever prompting to mine examples from internal analytics data, followed by manual verification, balancing cost inversely with harm prevalence. Fine-tuning is chosen over API usage for scale (cost, latency, throughput), maintainability, and access to output probability distributions. LoRA/QLoRA enable rapid single-GPU fine-tuning with megabyte-scale adapter weights. In production, LoRAX serves thousands of fine-tuned adapters on a single GPU, achieving tens of QPS at ~100ms latency on A10 GPUs for 7B parameter models, making marginal cost per adapter virtually zero. Heuristic gating and cascade classification via distillation further optimize throughput for high-frequency domains. Classification tasks benefit from requiring only one or a few output tokens, yielding low prediction latency and near 100% recall on simpler tasks. LLM generalization handles adversarial tactics (intentional typos, mixed characters, innuendos) better than traditional ML, slowing model staleness. Future directions include non-textual modalities using visual language models like LaMDA for explicit image detection, with the overarching vision of rapidly training and deploying adapters across the long tail of T&S violations for a safer platform.

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.summary: Vibhor Kumar introduces himself as a senior AI engineer at Tinder working on trust and safety for 5 years. He outlines the talk structure: what T&S is, GenAI's interaction with T&S, using LLMs for violation detection, and future outlook.

sections.title: What is Trust and Safety
sections.summary: T&S is more art than science, involving ethical judgment calls. Del Harvey's framework: prevent risk, reduce risk, detect harm, mitigate harm. Tinder focuses on detecting harm. As the largest dating app, it faces a long tail of violations from social media in profiles (high prevalence, low harm) to hate speech, harassment, and pig butchering scams (low prevalence, high harm).

sections.title: Problems GenAI Causes for T&S
sections.summary: GenAI enables content pollution (misinformation, spam), copyright inheritance, deepfake-enabled impersonation/catfishing/revenge porn, and scalable automated scam operations that defeat similarity/hash signals. T&S teams must increasingly use metadata signals (IP, ISP, phone numbers) and deal with LLM-automated messaging from fraudsters.

sections.title: Opportunities from Open-Source LLMs
sections.summary: Pre-trained open-source LLMs (Llama 3, Mistral) offer latent semantic capability and global language coverage. Fine-tuning achieves SOTA performance, sometimes beating few-shot GPT-4. Mature open-source tooling accelerates development from months to weeks. LLM generalization slows adversarial degradation curve significantly, obtained for free when using LLMs.

sections.title: Training Data Generation
sections.summary: Training data uses text-in/text-out format with prompts and classification labels. Only hundreds to thousands of examples needed. A hybrid approach uses GPT-4 with clever prompting to mine examples from internal analytics data (as auto-moderation), with cost inversely proportional to harm prevalence. Heuristics can restrict LLM calls to likely candidates. Manual verification fixes mislabeled data and handles ambiguous labels.

sections.title: Why Fine-Tune Instead of Using APIs
sections.summary: API LLMs don't scale for Tinder's real-time volume (cost, latency, throughput). Fine-tuning provides maintainability (control over weights, fine-tune on degradation), and access to output probability distributions for confidence metrics.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning Tools and PEFT
sections.summary: Open-source tools (Hugging Face, Axolotl, Ludwig, Llama Factory, H2O LLM Studio, Predibase) abstract fine-tuning to config files. LoRA freezes base weights, learning only megabytes of adapter weights, enabling rapid single-GPU experimentation. QLoRA unlocks fine-tuning largest models on one GPU. PEFT of larger base models outperforms full fine-tunes of smaller models for classification.

sections.title: Production Serving with LoRAX
sections.summary: LoRAX serves thousands of fine-tuned LoRA adapters on a single GPU by shuffling and batching adapters and requests. Marginal cost of a new adapter is virtually zero, enabling one adapter per harm type (hate speech, catfishing, pig butchering, etc.) without horizontal scaling. Special thanks to Predibase team.

sections.title: LoRAX Real-Time Performance and Optimizations
sections.summary: LoRAX optimizations enable real-time inference: 7B parameter models at tens of QPS with ~100ms latency on A10 GPUs. For high-frequency domains where this is insufficient, heuristic gating reduces request volume (e.g., only predicting on bios containing non-dictionary words). Cascade classification via distillation trains adapters on smaller base models optimizing for recall, invoking larger model adapters only when the smaller one gives a high enough score.

sections.title: LLM Classification Advantages and Generalization
sections.summary: Classification tasks require only one or a few output tokens, keeping time-to-prediction low despite auto-regressive generation. LLMs deliver massive precision/recall improvements over past NLP models, achieving near 100% recall on simpler tasks like social handle detection. Generalization is critical in the adversarial T&S game: LLMs handle intentional typos, mixed letters/numbers, and innuendos far better, making adapter-based models stale less quickly than traditional ML and providing stronger long-term defense.

sections.title: Future Directions and Conclusion
sections.summary: Future work explores non-textual modalities, including pre-trained visual language models like LaMDA for explicit image detection. The overarching vision: rapidly train adapters for the long tail of T&S violations using AI-in-the-loop dataset creation with policy experts, automate training/retraining pipelines, and leverage LoRAX to slot in new adapters at low marginal cost, building a next-generation defensive mode against harm for a safer, healthier platform.

limitations: Purely synthetic training examples risk not resembling true data distribution and are platform-agnostic.
Cost of GPT-4-based data mining is inversely proportional to true prevalence of harm.
T&S is more art than science, requiring ethical judgment calls.
Model performance degrades quickly in T&S due to adversarial nature of automated fraud.
LoRAX throughput on 7B models is sufficient for some but not all use cases, requiring heuristic gating or cascade classification for high-frequency domains.
